subject: MedNova audit: sample retention exemption and proof-of-deletion coordination
messages:
From: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@mednova.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: alex.gomez@mednova.com, compliance@mednova.com
Date: Sun, 4 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: sample retention exemption + proof-of-delete workflow

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our upcoming SOC 2 readiness review we need to validate a narrow retention exception for debug traces tied to our integration testing. Our standard requirement is 30 days for inference and debug telemetry; the auditors are asking for an exception to preserve a small subset of session traces for up to 90 days (only for tenants flagged as "test-audit").

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can implement a tenant-scoped retention override to 90 days for a named set of tenants?
- The mechanism you use to certify deletion when the exception window closes (proof-of-delete manifest or hash/timestamped artifact)?
- If any contractual/SA policy change is required for this exception?

We need evidence deliverables by May 12 so the auditor can sample artifacts. If helpful, I can share the auditor's checklist.

Appreciate a short reply and proposed timeline.

Best,
Sarah Turner
Head of Security Compliance, MedNova Therapeutics
[Attachment: mednova_audit_checklist.pdf (pdf)]

---
On Sun, 4 May 2025 at 11:03 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@mednova.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 4 May 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: sample retention exemption + proof-of-delete workflow

Thanks Sarah — looping in Kimberly (Security, SOC 2) and Marissa (Customer Success) so we can confirm the operational and contractual pieces. Quick answers up front:

- Tenant-scoped override: yes, we can apply a per-tenant TTL override on session/debug traces for a controlled set of tenants; it is gated by an exception policy.
- Proof-of-delete: we produce a tamper-evident manifest (timestamped entries + object hashes) and a signed confirmation from our retention pipeline once deletion completes; we can provide a CSV/manifest and a PDF attestation.
- Contract change: minor — we typically handle short-lived exceptions via an SOW or amendment rather than a full MSA redline; Security will confirm details.

Kimberly — can you confirm the conditions and whether we can commit artifacts by May 12? Also note the auditor may request the CAIQ/SIG mapping for our retention controls; Marissa can coordinate evidence delivery.

If it helps, I can stand up a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the exact artifacts.

-Karthik
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

On Mon, 5 May 2025 at 10:45 AM, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: sample retention exemption + proof-of-delete workflow

Karthik — thanks for the ping. Agreed we can support a controlled 90-day tenant override with the following conditions: 

1) Scope: exception limited to debug/session traces only (no full request/response payloads). A MedNova-maintained list of tenant IDs that will be flagged as "test-audit" is required.
2) Justification: MedNova must provide the auditor checklist and confirm sampling criteria.
3) Retention pipeline: we will label the objects with an exception flag and run the normal deletion job but skip flagged objects until the 90-day TTL expires.
4) Proof-of-delete: upon deletion run completion we will provide:
   - manifest CSV (object_id, tenant_id, deletion_timestamp, SHA256)
   - a PDF attestation signed by Redwood security (includes pipeline run id and link to internal job logs)
   - sample hashes (auditor can request up to 5 sample objects for verification).
5) Contract: operational exceptions for audits are covered by an amendment/SOW. Legal has advised a short addendum will suffice; Marissa can handle execution.
6) Audit window: we can commit to producing the artifacts within 5 business days of the deletion run. For May 12 deadline we need the list of tenant IDs by EOD May 6 and a DocuSign addendum executed by May 9.

Attachments we will provide: retention matrix (redwood_log-retention-matrix.xlsx), SOC 2 evidence snapshot (soc2-snapshot-202503.zip), and an example proof-of-delete manifest template. I will prepare the signed attestation after the deletion is completed.

Security note: hashed manifests are timestamped and stored in our evidence ledger (write-once). Any additional auditor requests beyond the 5 sample objects require an NDA amendment.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proof_of_delete_manifest_template.csv (csv)]

3) Evidence delivery: Assuming tenant list and signed addendum, Redwood will:
